From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: High tail latency on /generate during peak — impacting checkout

Update from triage (initial):
- Observed pattern: rapid increase in inflight requests between 08:05-08:20 PT. Queue depth for hosted-api pool r-hosted-1 climbed from median 5 to 120 concurrent queued requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: continuous batching combined with an edge burst of large sequence-length requests caused the runtime to form oversized batches. Oversized batches are triggering kernel slowdowns and KV cache thrash. This amplifies p95/p99 even though median token latency stays fine.
- Error rate: small uptick in 502/504 due to queue timeouts when worker slots saturated.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk):
1) Reduce max_batch_size and max_batch_latency for r-hosted-1 to force smaller, quicker batches.
2) Temporarily increase worker pool for r-hosted-1 (add 3 workers from warm pool).
3) Route Acme traffic to a dedicated, smaller-quantized variant (lower throughput but predictable tail).

I'm preparing the config patch and a runbook patch now. Will execute mitigation 1+2 as soon as we get thumbs-up — changes are reversible.

Attachments: sre_runbook.patch

—Dylan (SRE, Redwood)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T02:30:00Z
Subject: Re: High tail latency on /generate during peak — mitigation deployed

Triage & action log:
- 2027-05-11T02:30Z — Deployed config: max_batch_size reduced from 64->24, max_batch_latency from 25ms->10ms for r-hosted-1. Added 3 worker instances from warm pool.
- 2027-05-11T02:45Z — Observed queue depth drop from ~120 -> ~12 within 10 minutes. p95 improved from 1.6s -> ~200ms. p99 remains elevated (~1.1-1.6s) intermittently.
- 2027-05-11T03:20Z — Began routing 30% of Acme traffic to a quantized dedicated variant (r-dedicated-acme-v1) to reduce contention.

Notes: the p99 tail appears correlated with occasional long sequence-length requests that bypass prefix cache and force full KV reloads. Longer-term fixes: prepend request-size limits, improve prefix caching heuristics, and add adaptive batching based on sequence-length signals.

I'll keep monitoring through the next peak. If the customer requests, we can extend dedicated routing.

—Aditya Rao
Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
